definitions: A control method for AC electric motors that transforms the stator currents into a synchronously rotating reference frame, allowing for independent control of the magnetic flux and torque.
A vector control technique used to control the torque and speed of AC motors by independently controlling the flux and torque-producing components of the stator current.
examples: Field-oriented control is essential for high-performance motor drives.
The development of field-oriented control revolutionized AC motor applications.
Implementing field-oriented control requires precise current measurements.
